It is done, and submitted. You can play “Survival mode” or “Campaign mode”. If someone else wants to play, invite him. The game starts after being loaded, and you can quit in-game by pressing ESC button. You will also be able to press esc to exit and load the PTS later on.
Great experience, highly recommend!

Survival Mode:

In Survival mode, there are no static units spawned, but the spawn frequency is increased. 1 unit takes 5 times more damage than a normal infantry (the maximum damage, not always possible), 2 times longer to heal and twice as hard to kill compared to the same troop, that is the impact of the damage reduction on the game.

Survival mode vs The World: Infanterie

Campaign mode (solo):

In campaign mode, you get one player resource instead of support tanks and anti tanks only units. The campaign consists of 22 missions, each of which has four difficulties. The game is set the first few minutes, but once during a match you can choose difficult version.
You get the following things:

* 1 base resource
* 1 gold mine resource
* 2,25 uranium reserves (resource – get, lose capacity)
* 150 infantry resources
* 200 ammo (ammo – spend, get more ammo)

The difficulty increases gradually, so you do not get stuck in the campaign.

Campaign mode vs The World: Infanterie

Training
The training game lets you see how to position on the map and interact with nodes and buildings. A training map is also used in order to train the landing procedure and approach to the base.
When you are starting the campaign mode for the first time, there is a section in the training mode for warming up your troops.

Campaign mode (joint training mode):

Joint training mode

When playing campaign mode or Survival mode, you can invite people from the Steam Friends list. In the “friends” menu, you will now see all players playing the same mode and you can invite them to your game. When a friend receives an invitation to a public match and fails to respond, he is given the option to automatically join the existing offline game at the end of the matcheds. In case a friend accepts your invitation, he can join online from anywhere.
If you only want to play the game with a particular person, you can type his Steam name in the box “FILTER” in the “Choose an available game” menu.

Offline maps

At the start of an offline match, a number of conditions are applied:
1. All players must own at least one unit.
2. All players must have passed a training lesson. Training lesson is set to a number that corresponds to the distance of the closest training point.

The map is loaded as an offline game for the following modes:

* Survival mode (with other players)
* Survival Solo (survival Solo is offline)
* Campaign mode (with other players)
* Campaign Solo (training or campaign Solo is offline)
* Solo vs the World (training or Solo vs the World is offline)
* Trainer / Trainer 2

How should a training map look like?
I have worked out a form of training that I find interesting, for example, it has some units and buildings that are not subject to protection in the starting position as a shelter. This means that it is difficult for the enemy to attack in places that are important for the player. Here is both a map of a training map that is easy to build (05-06:35) and its form:

As shown, the training map is much larger than a standard map. Here, the player has enough space to train as well. I think that a map of this form is good for learning to understand where certain units spawn and to what extent the distance affects the flight time of the troops and time for recovery.

On the screen above you can see a training map that I like to use. There are various features of the map, one of which is shown in the picture below.
The red lines on the map represent nodes of the order system that have been switched off (not in the game). This means that in offline training it is difficult to win the map. At the moment, I just build nodes, but I want to build a form of the training, as much as possible in the form of a campaign or Survival mode.

In the training map, there is a bunker on the left where players can gather before they enter the game. The bunker is connected to the training camp, where the units are stationed, and to the production center. Here is our final training map.
Here, the training map of some important situations that emerge on the map (in offline training).

To the Left from the production center an anti-aircraft defense.
Behind the training camp there are two enemy cannons. In the bottom of the map, there are two types of trenches.

Q: What's the simplest way to pass a timedelta as input for a vbscript task? A: Take a look at how I do it: if Err.Number = 0 then call myTask.InputParams = 6 * hourPattern End if Note that there is a good reason for being explicit about vbscript parameters. You can get a reference that gives some detail on that in "Functions in a SET or INPUT parameter". The point is that vbscript variables aren't necessarily implicitly created as a task parameter. Q: Is there a way to determine a date from an ISO8601 representation string? A: http://support.microsoft.com/kb/241051 http://www.w3schools.com/php/php_date_isodate.asp The best alternative is to use the java webstart api's DateFormat to get or set the date/time as used by the wsclient. http://java.sun.com/j2se/1.5.0/docs/api/java/text/SimpleDateFormat.html http://java.sun.com/j2se/1.5.0/docs/api/java/text/DateFormat.html the most general parameter is the java.text.SimpleDateFormat which takes constructor parameters that correspond to the important fields in ISO-8601. The pattern "MM-dd-yyyy hh:mm:ss z" corresponds to '25-03-2006 07:13:31 GMT'. (There is also a java.text.DateFormat used to set and get the value from the task. Q: How do I construct a task that sets the list of users for a group? A: (It should go without saying that this is a very silly question, but if you don't ask you don't know, right?) You will need a task intended to get at the directory service, something like this: WSHCommand( "\wsclient -usersUser=SambaUser -userid $userid -groups %r -r $task.TaskDirectory -r $DirectoryService -r $TaskLogLevel -r $TaskList " ) Where -userid $userid is for setting the UserID to the directory service, and -r $ListSegments is for setting the content of that list. There may be ways to use a single task (direct access to the text lines in the task), but this seemed easiest. The thing to be aware of is that to be useful in the controller you will have to translate an RBAC Group into usernames. On-board tasks for the vbscript type controller are: Note that any TaskHandler can get or set TaskLogLevel and TaskList. Q: Is there a way to limit a task to a specific group, domain, or namespace? A: The best way to accomplish this would be to write a taskhandler specifically for the type of object in question (or the type subclass that they use). There is no direct mechanism for limiting access to individual objects to a group. When the 1.44 release comes out I'm not certain that there will be any way other than vbscript to limit scope beyond a tasklog. Q: Is there a way to test both read-only and write operations against a task log? A: Yes. The syntax for specifying an access policy type has been modified so that both 1 and 0 (read-only, deny, etc.) will produce a TaskLock.cs exception according to what was specified. Q: What's the simplest wsclient code to access the registry under the following conditions? 1. A) The value is not a folder handle nor can be set by wsclient (Must I create a separate task?) B) The setting is a boolean, also under the following condition: A.1 The setting is read-only A.2 I can change the value only via the task handler provided. A.1 TaskHandler.Access = 10 A.2 TaskHandler.Write = 0 Q: What's the simplest way to write to the registry using the wsclient.tasks module? A: First example. Look up "task handler". Second example. wsclient.TaskHandler(" RegistryOperation","name=HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Samba\\ServiceSettings\\SambaClient",access='r'){ task=TaskHandle task. taskhandler = 'RegistryOperation' task.TaskLogLevel = 0 task.TaskName='logdir' task.TaskHandlerLogLevel = 0 task.ListOfChanges =FALSE task.Value={{'SambaClient':{'Mode' '0'}}} task.UpdateMode = 1 task.

What does this commit solve?

The test calls the 1. MySql interface for a typed parameter with default. commit 42b805c08571b83209afc708b63707f56266c248 seems to not do this. So I'm making this PR on the assumption that we don't want to add more ways to handle this but I'm still undecided. A few version notes in the doc too. jOOQ does not rely on the MySQL 5.6 API, we use the one that happens to be present, no matter which version is present. We also add 5.0 or 5.1 compatible APIs when we think you need it in a given environment.The commit with this PR changes that as we now don't go overboard and make things that 5.0+ do to appear to the client as well as the client that is 5.0+ or higher. This works for all MySQL servers and 5.0 or greater and if we must go down, it will just work with a different option. @j0rgey is this the expected behaviour?
If you want to support that, you can use object == null && default == null as well to get this behavior.
It is the expected behaviour. The first version of this PR used isset. The PR has changed to work with null values as well. As the second part of this commit, I also added support for the limitation that was in MySQL 5.6. Also, I updated the initial testing of 5.1. Here is the other matching commit: This commit now builds the mysql node package and bump up support for the latest MySQL version. We also improved the jOOQ's type detection functionality that makes sure for each operation we call the relevant API (depending on the operation, either uppers/lowers case or the data type). This PR is pretty straight-forward; we just bump the latest MySQL version that we support from 5.6 to 5.7. This commit has many smaller changes. I've split them into logical groups.
